lawyer:
Mr. A.F. Hassan Ariff, Senior Advocate, instructed by Mr. Md. Ahsan Ullah Patwary, Advocate-on-Record ------ for the Petitioners. 
Mr. S.M. Fazlul Huq (in person) ------ for the Respondent

Mongla Port Authority and another
Vs.
S.M. Fazlul Huq
full_judgment:
2. The facts revealed in the leave petition, in short, are that the respondent as plaintiff instituted aforesaid suit stating, inter alia, that the petitioner joined service in the year 1981 as a Deputy Secretary under Mongla Port Authority and worked with full satisfaction of the Authority and applied for the Post of Secretary but due to Young age he was appointed as Deputy Secretary of Mongla Port Authority. That he earlier served in Planning Commission and as Principal of a College of Noakhali and also got training in Holland and in total rendered 24 years of public service. That the petitioner was unnecessarily harassed being an honest officer and he was willfully deprived of his rights by Mongla Port Authority. On 03.03.1985 petitioner was terminated from service and also was entangled in criminal Cases and also suspended on different occasions. A gang in Mongla Port Authority was involved in defalcation of crores of Taka which was reported by Parliamentary Standing Committee and accordingly different officers of Mongla Port Authority were found guilty for the defalcation and cases were field against them with the Bureau of Anti Corruption. The Plaintiff filed Suit against his termination, suspension and got decrees in the suits and four appeals were favourably disposed of in the High Court Division of in his favour and he was released from criminal and Anti Corruption cases so he filed two Suits being Money Suit No. 103 of 1994 and Money Suit No. 3 of 1997 in the Court of Subordiante Judge, Bagerhat seeking damages and compensation. In this way, 13/14 years of plaintiffs service life were lost. The plaintiffs termination order, departmental Proceedings were declared illegal by Subordinate Judge, Bagerhat in Title Suit No. 22 of 1990 and three departmental proceeding were declared illegal in Title Suit No. 18 of 1990 and Title Suit No. 32 of 1992 in the Court of the Assistant Judge, Mongla. As plaintiffs junior Baud Ali was promoted and the plaintiff was posted to a lower Post as Deputy Secretary the plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 4 of 1990 in the Court of the Assistant Judge, Mongla when the Court declared that he was still in service either in the Post of Manager (Administration) or Secretary (Board and public relations). Mongla Port Authority did not implement the order but later reinstated him on 08.12.1997. He was declared to be entitled to promotion in the Post of Director (Administration) or any other Post but Mongla Port Authority filed Title Appeal No. 196 of 1993 in Bagerhat District Judge's Court against the order and the Said Order was stayed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 26423 of 1994 and the order of promotion was not made effective. In 1998-99 Parliamentary standing Committee on Ministry of Shipping made inquiry and there the fact of harassment of plaintiff was narrated and plaintiff was recommended for promotion. The committee declared that appointment of director (Administration) of Mongla Port Authority on deputation is illegal but as all Administrative actions of Mongla Port Authority were operated from the Office of Director (Administration) of Mongla Port Authority on deputation is illegal but as all Administrative actions of Mongla Port Authority were operated from the Office of Director (Administration) so the plaintiff was harassed by them and he was transferred on 28.02.1999 and as his juniors were promoted on 08.12.1997, so his right was hampered. The defendants have not prepared any gradation list as per Mongla Port Authority Service Rule 1991. The plaintiff was shown senior in 1992 by Parliamentary Committee of Government Offices at Page 39 of their report. But plaintiffs name was written in different papers under his junior so he was shocked. Still different Suits, Appeals, Civil Revision etc. were continuing between plaintiff and defendants and the defendants have not implemented full judgment and that in such state of affairs the order of removal was claimed to be illegal. When a Title Execution Case was pending the removal of plaintiff on 27.09.2000 without any notice is nothing but contempt of Court, so the plaintiff filed contempt Case No. 01 of 2000 the Court of the Assistant Judge, Mongla. The plaintiff has been terminated/removed disregarding the Service Rule, Ministry's Order and Parliamentary Standing Committee Report. Plaintiffs wife and Children are educated so his removal caused mental disturbance to the family, which removal is also willful victimization. The plaintiff was earlier also reinstated as per Court's order and he was not given his seniority and every one in Mongla Port Authority is torturing him and thus he was removed on 27.09.2000 which is nothing but an order of dismissal and such order is unfair, partism and without any basis and liable to be declared illegal. The defendant not only removed him but tried to forcibly evict him from his quarter so he and his family members are in a panic and the plaintiffs case has merit and he has prima-facie case so the order of removal dated 27.09.2000 is liable to be stayed. The defendants by misuse of power passed order of removal without show cause notice in violation of natural justice so the order is not valid and the order was passed by defendant No. 2 on 27.09.2000 due to personal grudge for attachment order against him. The Director (Administration) of Mongla Port Authority on 18.04.2000 got additional charge of Senior Accounts Officer and became powerful and Administration was run by him and on the other side on 25.01.2000 news of forgery of Certificates of Private Secretary of defendant No. 2 was flashed in the News papers as plaintiff put up file for examination of Certificates of Private Secretary so all became annoyed with the plaintiff but plaintiff was removed illegally. As plaintiff demanded implementation of previous decrees and on 27.09.2000 the Assistant Judge, Mongla passed order of attachment of official goods of defendants in Title Suit No. 04 of 1993, so on receipt of that order when attachment order was to be executed the plaintiff was served with a Memo dated 27.09.2000 thus removing him from the service of Mongla Port Authority. The plaintiff treat the letter as dismissal and the letter is victimization of decree holder plaintiff. The order has been made effective on 24 years of furnishing of public service by plaintiff so the order is liable to set aside and the authority cannot remove the plaintiff without show cause and he has been serving in high post and inspite of having age of service, his removal is illegal, victimization etc., and as plaintiff served Legal Notice as per Section 49 of Mongla Port Authority Ordinance 1976 and as the defendants did not reply so a Suit can be filed after one month but the defendant on 07.11.2000 replied the notice but did not give reliefs as prayed for so the plaintiff filed the Suit. 

 3. The petitioners contested the suit by filing written statement and denying the material allegations made in the plaint. It was stated that the suit was not maintainable and he was terminated as per service rule and that he was appointed directly on 31.10.1981 without any advertisement by the then Chairman of Mongla Port Authority and thereafter he was posted as Deputy Chief Planning and that the then Chairman appointed the plaintiff with a scale of Tk. 1400-2225 that the plaintiff was entitled to pay at the scale of Tk. 750-1470 and so the plaintiff was found to have joined the service exercising illegal influence and he worked in excess to service rule and so he was terminated and that there were criminal cases against the plaintiff and considering the facts and circumstances he was legally terminated and so the suit was liable to be dismissed. 

 4. The Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Bagerhat after considering the materials on record including the evidence decreed the suit declaring the termination order of the plaintiff dated 27 September 2000 to be illegal and declaring that the plaintiff was entitled to get outstanding salary. The appeal preferred by the petitioner was also dismissed. Thereafter the petitioner moved the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 2534 of 2002 and the High Court Division by the impugned judgment and order discharged the rule. Hence is this petition. 

 7. We have considered the submission made by the learned Counsel and perused the materials on record. It appears that the trial court considered that the plaintiff was terminated from his job on various grounds including involvement in criminal cases for corruption but it appears that he has been exonerated from the criminal cases. 

 8. Further allegation against the plaintiff was that the plaintiff made direct correspondence with the Chairman of the defendant petitioner No. 1 and as such this conduct was found unbecoming and so he was terminated under Rule 55 of Mongla Port Authority Employees rules, 1991. 

 9. It further appears that after being exonerated from criminal cases the plaintiff instituted other suit No. 4 of 1990 and the suit was decreed against the defendant petitioners and so he started Execution Case No. 3 of 1993 and in the aforesaid Execution Case Order of attachment of 50% salary of the defendant No. 2 was made and also an order for attaching his official articles was made and this enraged the authorities and out of malice the order purported to be dated 28.09.2000 was issued terminating the plaintiff from the service. The aforesaid facts and circumstances including proximity of time leads an irresistible opinion as to attempt of victimizing the plaintiff (order of attachment was passed on 27.09.2000 and order of removal was issued by memo dated 28.09.2000). It appears from the judgment of the trial court that the evidence of the parties was considered and though it was alleged on behalf of the defendant that the action against the plaintiff was taken on the basis of a report of the Joint Secretary of the Ministry but the said report nor even a copy thereof was produced before the court thereby the trial court correctly held that the impugned memo of removal was without any legal basis. The lower appellate court on the other hand considered the materials on record including the evidence. It was found that the plaintiff succeeded in 14 cases against the defendant and that the allegation of corruption against the plaintiff could not be established as the plaintiff admittedly has been released from the aforesaid charge of corruption. The contention of the defendants that by making direct correspondence with the Chairman of the defendant No. 1 the plaintiff committed misconduct, on the face of materials on record and the circumstances noticed, above does not inspire us to hold adverse opinion against the respondent in this regard. 

 10. From the facts and circumstances it appears that the plaintiff has been thrown out of service in the name of termination, but in fact from the trend of victimization meted out to the plaintiff, he has been removed under the garb of termination. The lower appellate court after consideration of the materials on record held:- 

 11. It appears that trial court as well as the court of appeal below concurrently found that the plaintiff was entangled in criminal cases from which he has been exonerated and that he filed a number of cases against the defendant successfully and that in view of Execution Case No. 3 of 1993 the plaintiff succeeded to obtain an order of attachment of the salary and office goods of the defendant No. 2 on 27.09.2000-all these, amongst others, to led to create a sense of venom in the minds of the defendant No. 2 as a result of which the plaintiff has been victimized by the defendant issuing the impugned memo in fact removing him on 28.09.2000. Thus the aforesaid action of removal has been found to be illegal by both the courts below. The High Court Division in its turn affirmed the judgment. 

 12. Before we part with, we like to add that though we are not inclined to interfere with the ultimate result of the judgments of the High Court Division as well as of the courts below, but we do not see eye to eye to the observation made by them that in case of termination any notice of show cause is necessary. Since we have found on the basis of materials on record, that the action taken against the plaintiff is malafide we do not like to interfere in the ultimate result of the impugned judgments.
